title: AnotherOddThing: resident computation, active probes and local learning regimes
summary: A focused archaeology pass for AnotherOddThing. The repository explicitly says it was spun out of AnttisNeuron, GrowingAnttisNeuron, ActiveVectorNN and FusionMachine, then turns several recurring Genealogy themes into falsifiable toy mechanisms: computation resident at the destination, tiny addressed interventions that reveal hidden operators, compartment-shared state for expression/plasticity coordination, and destructive controls that progressively narrow which local state is actually required. Cross-links to GeometricNeuronV24 and ReadWrite are recorded as recurring mechanisms, not invented ancestry.

nodes.claim: A small addressed event can expose or perturb computation already resident at its destination, while compartment-local state constrains both present expression and future plasticity; the project then attacks each stronger interpretation with matched controls.
nodes.survived: The durable core is resident computation plus addressed intervention plus local learning coordinates. v0 shows passive equality can hide different resident operators until a known hidden-site poke; v1 turns the poke into bounded active identification; v2-v3 show that coordinating expression and plasticity through local compartment state and thresholded update regimes can matter under routing/set-point mismatch.
nodes.killed: Several richer stories are deliberately narrowed. A separate perfectly mirrored plasticity trace matches the shared trace, so object sharing itself buys nothing. The v4 matched attacker further shows that the 15/45 ms two-timescale plasticity trace is not necessary for the current level-only set-point knee: a calibrated single scalar preserves the same qualitative transition, leaving fast-minus-slow temporal contrast to earn its keep on a task that actually reads it.

edges.why: AnotherOddThing explicitly states that it was spun out of AnttisNeuron; the inherited question is how local neuron-like structure changes the meaning of a small event without making the event carry the whole computation.
AnotherOddThing explicitly names GrowingAnttisNeuron as an origin. The shared residue is that developed/local structure can determine later response even when a message itself is small.

AnotherOddThing explicitly names ActiveVectorNN as an origin and keeps its separation between rich resident state/computation and sparse events, but turns the event into a controlled probe as well as an update.

AnotherOddThing explicitly names FusionMachine as an origin. The later repo strips the machine question down to resident dynamics, addressed perturbation and local transduction so each mechanism can be attacked separately.

motifs.title: The message can be smaller than the computation it selects
motifs.description: ActiveVectorNN separates persistent state from sparse events; GeometricNeuronV24 and ReadWrite make bounded measurement/addressed intervention part of identifiability; AnotherOddThing closes the triangle by holding an operator resident and using a tiny known poke to reveal response structure that passive observation cannot see. These are recurring mechanisms, not a claim that V24 or ReadWrite are AnotherOddThing's parents.

motifs.title: Local state can select how future transfer is allowed to change
motifs.description: AnttisNeuron and GrowingAnttisNeuron keep computation tied to local physical/structural state. AnotherOddThing isolates a smaller version: compartment state feeds a thresholded no-change/LTD/LTP regime and branch-wide normalization. Its destructive controls then show that the categorical regime survives as a useful object while the particular 15/45 ms two-timescale implementation is not necessary for the present level-only task.
